podcast.title: Accomplished Field Hockey Player
podcast.body: While a student at King's College, London, Chris Martin of Coldplay was an accomplished field hockey player. Despite his skill, his team referred to him by the unusual nickname "Pookecy." "Chris Martin, a cold play, was quite the field hockey player while at University at King's College, London."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Ambidextrousness and Creative Approach
podcast.body: Chris Martin is ambidextrous, writing with his left hand and drawing with his right, a trait suggested as a potential factor for his unique approach to the piano. This specific brain function is thought to contribute to the distinctive and different musical outcomes he achieves on the instrument. "He's amdextrous. While he writes with his left hand, he draws with his right. If your brain works this way, it kind of makes sense that when you sit down at a piano, things are going to come out differently."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Musical Influences and Discovery of Piano
podcast.body: Chris Martin grew up influenced by artists such as U2, the Norwegian band A-ha, and Michael Jackson, largely due to his father's musical tastes. At age 11, while at boarding school, he discovered the piano through his teacher Mark Tanner, a concert pianist with an appreciation for pop and rock, leading his parents to buy him his own keyboard. "He grew up listening to a lot of You Too, Aha, the Norwegian band, and Michael Jackson, thanks to his dad who was also a big music band. At age 11, he was sent off to boarding school, where he had a teacher named Mark Tanner. Tanner was a professional concert pianist who also had an appreciation for Pop and Rock. It was through him that Chris discovered the piano."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Exceptional Pianist Despite Inability to Read Music
podcast.body: Chris Martin is regarded as an excellent pianist, not primarily for technical skill, but for his exceptional creativity and "ear familiarly." Despite his inability to read music, his work with the piano is described as "quite extraordinary," highlighting his innate musicality. "He can't read music, believe it or not, but what he does with a piano is quite extraordinary."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Formation of Coldplay at University
podcast.body: Chris Martin's significant career break occurred when he enrolled at University College London, where he met his future Coldplay bandmates: Johnny Buckland, Guy Berryman, and Will Champion. This meeting was pivotal in the formation of one of the most commercially successful piano-based alt rock bands. "The big break came when he entered University College, London, where he met cold play bandmates Johnny Buckland, Guy Berryman, and Will Champion."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influenced by Jeff Buckley
podcast.body: Chris Martin is specifically mentioned as one of the singers who was deeply impacted by Jeff Buckley's intimate music, highlighting Buckley's lasting repercussion on later generations of artists and their vocal styles. xref.title: Ancestor Invented Daylight Savings Time
xref.body: Chris Martin's great-great-grandfather is credited with originating the concept of daylight savings time, an idea that emerged prior to World War I. "The great, great grandfather of Cold Placing or Chris Martin is the guy who came up with the concept of daylight savings time in the days before World War I."

xref.title: Blood-Infused Vinyl Edition
xref.body: For their 2012 Record Store Day release, "Hetty Fwins," The Flaming Lips created a special clear vinyl edition that visibly contained traces of the band's blood. They also extended this practice to their collaborators, demanding that artists like Chris Martin of Coldplay, Kesha, and Yoko Ono contribute their own blood for ten ultra-rare special editions of the record. "Not only did the clear vinyl vividly show traces of flaming lips blood, but the band also demanded that any of the collaborators on this record also contribute their precious bodily fluid for 10 special editions of the record."

xref.title: Goofy Song for Chris Martin's Child
xref.body: Coldplay formed the pseudonymous band The Nappys to record a goofy song and accompanying video called "I'm Your Baby's Daddy." This project was a personal endeavor by Chris Martin, dedicated to his then-wife Gwyneth Paltrow while she was expecting their first child, affectionately referred to as "Little Apple." Sir George Martin notably introduced the video in a curly red wig. "When she was expecting Little Apple, the band got together for a goofy song and video under the name The Nappy's."

xref.title: Most Commercially Successful Piano-Based Alt Rock Band
xref.body: Coldplay is widely considered the most commercially successful piano-based band to emerge from the alt rock genre. Their success is largely driven by Chris Martin's use of the piano as his primary instrument, which features prominently in many of their hit songs. "The most commercially successful piano based band to come out of the Al Rock world is arguably cold play."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Piano as Central to Band's Sound
xref.body: The piano serves as Chris Martin's primary instrument, making it integral to Coldplay's distinctive sound. Its prominent inclusion in many of the band's biggest songs defines their musical identity within the alt rock landscape. "The piano is, after all, Chris Martin's primary instrument, and that's why many of the band's big songs involve the piano."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.body: Tim Rice-Oxley, a skilled piano player, was asked by Chris Martin to join his band, Coldplay, but Tim declined the offer. He believed that Keane had a better chance of success. "By this time, Tim Rice Oxley was a pretty good piano player, and some dude named Chris Martin was so impressed. He had asked him to join his band, which was called Coldplay. Tim thought that Keene was a better bat, so he said no to Chris."
